content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 273 (Powers of Tribunal). On a winding-up petition the Tribunal may dismiss it, make an interim order, appoint a provisional liquidator, make a winding-up order, or any other order it thinks fit. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: An order is made within the period the section states. Before appointing a provisional liquidator the Tribunal gives notice to the company unless the circumstances justify otherwise. The grounds for the petition are section 271.
